title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
disposition_detail: The SJC sustained the complaint and annulled the contumacy judgment, excommunication, Session actions of July 2 and July 16, and Presbytery action of August 11. Thompson returned to membership under the still-pending indictment. The trespass warning was not before the SJC.
first_summary: The SJC sustained Thompson’s complaint and annulled his pretrial contumacy judgment and excommunication. His conduct did not constitute the objectively demonstrated contumacy immediately censurable under BCO 32-6, and no mutually acceptable BCO 38-1 confession existed. He was restored to membership with the original indictment still pending.
summary: After a Session excommunicated a member without trial for contumacy, the SJC sustained his complaint and annulled the contumacy judgment, excommunication, and later Session and Presbytery actions. No mutually agreed BCO 38-1 confession existed, and declining a confession meeting was not immediately censurable objective contumacy under BCO 32-6; subjective contumacy required confession or trial. He reverted to membership under pending indictment. The SJC did not find the indictment unconstitutional, decide trial guilt, or consider the unpleaded trespass warning.
